title: Chief cult-part: invocation—Saints know at least what touches their beatitude, including living prayers for their help
source_text: XL. Sed praecipua pars cultus qui Sanctis hominibus & Angelis impenditur in Ecclesia Romana consistit in eorum invocatione, & precibus quae ad illos diriguntur, tum voce, tum etiam solo cordis affectu, & interna mentis loquela. Qua de re ut accuratius teneatur Scholae Romanae Doctrina, observandum est Theologos illius communiter supponere Sanctos cum Christo regnantes, non quidem omnia & singula quae hic geruntur nosse; sed ea saltem omnia quae ad ipsorum beatitudinem pertinent & faciunt. Ad Sanctorum autem Beatitudinem facere existimant, ut noscant cultum qui illis exhibetur, & preces ac orationes, quibus fideles in terris degentes ad eorum opem confugiunt. Ac proinde apud istos Theologos certum est, Sanctos defunctos viventium preces percipere & intelligere.
pass_a_gloss: But the chief part of the cult which is paid to holy men and Angels in the Roman Church consists in their invocation, and in prayers which are directed to them, both by voice and also by the affection of the heart alone, and by the interior speech of the mind. On which matter, that the Doctrine of the Roman School may be more accurately held, it is to be observed that its Theologians commonly suppose that the Saints reigning with Christ do not indeed know all and singular things that are done here; but at least all those things which pertain to and make for their beatitude. But they judge it makes for the Beatitude of the Saints that they know the cult which is exhibited to them, and the prayers and orations by which the faithful living on earth flee to their help. And therefore among those Theologians it is certain that the deceased Saints perceive and understand the prayers of the living.
pass_b_english: Invocation is the chief Roman cult of Saints and Angels—spoken aloud or by heart alone.
School premise: reigning Saints need not know all earthly events, yet know what touches their beatitude—including cult and pleas for their aid.
Hence it is certain for them that the dead Saints hear the living’s prayers.
Slice closes at XL; next frontier is Romana XLI–LXXVII (how they hear; merits; patrons; Marian dominion), then Pars Secunda Reformata.

lemmas.gloss: to perceive and understand the prayers of the living
